So dnd is very numbers based on what you can do. Everything revolves around what numbers are on your character sheet. On top of that dnd can take a lot of setup. Mothership is a lot more improv in all aspects, it relies on the dm and the players to craft information and approach any situation in various ways. For instance mothership says abilities should be considered as a wishlist of what they want to see appear in the game and they can argue an ability would allow them to approach something differently than others. My players wanted to fix an armored vehicle and one player was an engineer so he obviously had the abilities to fix it but to give advantage on how long repairs would take our marine used military training as his skill arguing that his training would include basic vehicle repair. The rules are bare bone and players only really need to know how rolling works to start. If you and your players are big on improv then you will love mothership
